papers.title_en: Rethinking the Role of Feature Engineering and Learning Strategies in Few-Shot Hidden Emotion Recognition
papers.authors: Xiaochuan Guo, Jihao Gu, Haixu Liu, Yuxin Liu, Qi Wang, Yufei Wang, Fei Wang, Kun Li, Dan Guo
papers.evidence: 多模态时序建模框架，用于视频中隐藏情感识别
papers.tldr: 针对长视频中隐藏情感证据弱且稀疏的问题，提出紧凑多模态时间建模框架，集成2D/3D骨架、面部表情Blendshapes、DINOv2/v3等多种特征。采用交叉注意力机制，以静态姿势特征为Query、动态微动特征为Key/Value，消除个体静态偏差，结合多实例学习自适应池化提取瞬时情感。在EI-MIGA-IJCAI挑战赛Track 3中以0.76923准确率获第一，并揭示通用视觉基础模型在微动态任务中的表示崩溃与伪泛化机制。贡献在于重新思考特征工程与学习策略在小样本隐藏情感识别中的关键作用。
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we present the solution developed by our team, XInsight Lab, which achieved first place in Track 3 of the 4th EI-MIGA-IJCAI Challenge with a test accuracy of 0.76923. To address the challenge of weak and sparse implicit emotion evidence in long videos, this paper extends the winning solution from the previous competition and proposes a compact multi-modal temporal modeling framework. The framework integrates and evaluates the effects of multi-source features, including 2D/3D skeletons, facial expression Blendshapes, DINOv2/v3 vision foundation models, X-CLIP video features, and Gemini semantic priors. Architecturally, we propose a cross-attention mechanism that utilizes static pose features, denoted as Base, as the Query and dynamic micro-motion differential features, denoted as Offset, as the Key and Value. By capturing local relative velocities, this mechanism eliminates static biases related to individual body shape and identity. Concurrently, an adaptive pooling method based on Multiple Instance Learning is employed to extract instantaneous emotions while suppressing background noise in long sequences. Finally, the paper reveals the representation collapse phenomenon of general vision foundation models in micro-dynamic tasks, and analyzes the underlying mechanisms where networks fall into public-leaderboard-driven pseudo-generalization due to shortcut learning and rote memorization.

papers.title_en: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.authors: Chungpa Lee, Jihoon Kwon, Kyle Min, Jy-yong Sohn
papers.evidence: 跨模态特征异质性分析，支持解耦表示
papers.tldr: 视觉语言模型的联合嵌入空间存在特征纠缠，稀疏自编码器（SAE）用于解耦但隐含跨模态特征方向一致的假设。本文发现图像和文本中相同概念的特征方向存在异质性，导致模态分裂。通过训练模态特定SAE保留各自几何结构，再事后对齐特征，提升了重建保真度与跨模态检索、概念引导性能。该研究揭示了特征异质性是模态分裂的关键，为跨模态解耦提供了更有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models map images and text into a joint embedding space. However, these embeddings often entangle multiple semantic features, which limits their interpretability and controllability. While sparse autoencoders have emerged as a useful tool for decomposing these embeddings into monosemantic features, their application to joint embedding spaces has largely relied on an implicit, untested assumption that semantically corresponding features share the same directions across modalities. In this paper, we challenge this assumption by identifying discrepancies in feature directions for the same concept across image and text modalities, a phenomenon we term cross-modal feature heterogeneity. We demonstrate that this heterogeneity is a key driver of the modality split, where a shared concept activates different latents depending on the modality. This finding further reveals why aligning latent activations alone is insufficient to resolve the underlying feature mismatch. Motivated by this observation, we propose an approach that trains modality-specific sparse autoencoders to preserve each modality's feature geometry, and then aligns corresponding features post hoc. Our method improves reconstruction fidelity and enhances performance in cross-modal retrieval and concept steering.

papers.title_en: Forewarned is Forearmed: When Non-Sequential Embedding Turns Into an Anomaly Detector
papers.authors: Elys Allesiardo, Antoine Caubrière, Valentin Vielzeuf
papers.evidence: 多模态句子级嵌入分析
papers.tldr: 多模态句子级嵌入（如SONAR）的某些维度对扰动敏感，可指示解码异常。通过利用连续编码与解码之间的一致性，本文构建了一个精确的异常检测器。此外，还探索了修改特定嵌入维度以尝试纠正异常。该工作强调分析嵌入本身对增强多模态表示可靠性的关键作用。
papers.abstract_en: This paper offers an in-depth analysis of non-sequential multimodal sentence-level embeddings, with a particular focus on the SONAR model. We demonstrate that certain embedding dimensions are sensitive to perturbations and can serve as indicators of decoding anomalies. By leveraging the consistency between successive encoding and decoding, we successfully build an accurate detector. Additionally, we explore modifying specific dimensions of interest to attempt to correct them. This work underscores the importance of understanding and analyzing the embeddings themselves to enhance the reliability of multimodal representations.
